account:
Today I have ordinary office business at eight, a mill grain inspection at ten, council letters after lunch, and tea with my neighbour at fifteen. Something unusual may also be taking shape around the great hall. The builder and innkeeper were at the office unusually early this morning, and the builder, carrying a lantern, has asked me to meet him at the hall entrance at 17:55 and step inside at 18:00 for a brief inspection of lighting and hall arrangements. I accepted; the secretary has asked for explicit approval to amend the office period. I have asked the builder what specifically needs inspecting and have not yet heard an explanation.

Yesterday I noticed the innkeeper carrying a sack of bread at town hall. That might simply be ordinary inn supplies. My neighbour reported the baker's explanation that there was no celebration or decorating, perhaps just his oven glowing, and knew of no visitors or gatherings. The secretary had no verified news of public importance and no new accounts or correspondence. None of this establishes a hidden event. Still, the bread, early visit, and carefully timed hall appointment make me wonder whether a gathering is being arranged, possibly a surprise involving me, rather than merely routine maintenance. The builder is directly involved in the proposed inspection, and the secretary is handling its scheduling; I do not know whether the innkeeper or baker has any connection. I intend to keep my appointments and learn more through direct questions and observation rather than treat suspicion as fact.
